identified.name: FIPS Overlay Advert
identified.app_or_protocol: FIPS (Free Internetworking Peering System) mesh network; most publishers are Iris web clients via fips-ts
identified.what_it_is: Addressable 'overlay advert' that a FIPS node signs with its identity key (the Nostr key is the network identity) to publish how it can be reached. Tags: d and protocol = the rendezvous app id (spec default 'fips-overlay-v1'; 19/20 samples use 'iris-client'), version '1', NIP-40 expiration ~1h. Content JSON {identifier, version, endpoints:[{transport: udp|tcp|tor|webrtc, addr}], stunServers?, signalRelays?}. NAT hole-punch signaling then runs over NIP-59 gift-wrapped kind 21059 to the peer's kind 10050 inbox relays.
identified.notes: Largest by authors in this batch (2,410 authors / 2,825 events) — almost all are Iris browser sessions using protocol='iris-client' with transport 'webrtc' and addr = the node's compressed secp256k1 pubkey. Pure P2P signalling noise for a social client; Amethyst only needs it if it ever joins the FIPS mesh. Sibling kind 37196 is the paid exit-route offer.

identified.name: Double Ratchet message
identified.what_it_is: Signal-style Double Ratchet DM message (MESSAGE_EVENT_KIND = 1060). Signed by an ephemeral ratchet key (not the user's identity key); a `header` tag carries the NIP-44-encrypted ratchet header (next sender pubkey, message counters), a `p` tag points at the recipient's current ratchet pubkey, and content is the ratcheted ciphertext of an inner unsigned rumor (kind 14 chat, 7 reaction, 15 receipt, 25 typing, 10448 chat settings). Invites travel as kind 30078 (d `double-ratchet/invites`) and invite responses as kind 1059.
identified.notes: Largest kind in the batch (93k events, 1.4k authors). Each author is a throwaway ratchet key, so the author count says little about the number of real users. The same kind is also used for group sender-key messages. Supporting it would make Amethyst interoperate with Iris Chat DMs. It needs the ratchet state machine, not just an event class.

identified.name: Unidentified fixed-size ephemeral-key packets
source_urls: GitHub code search for 4333 + nostr (only UUID false positives)
identified.what_it_is: Every event is signed by a fresh throwaway key (637 events / 637 authors), carries one `z` tag (16-byte hex, only a handful of distinct values shared across authors) and an `expiration` exactly 121 s after created_at. The content is NOT NIP-44: it is a fixed 347-byte binary frame `0x01 | 16 random bytes | the 16-byte z value | 4-byte big-endian expiration timestamp | 0x03 0x01 0x33 | 307 opaque bytes`. Batches for each z value arrive in lockstep every 1-2 minutes, which looks like mixnet/cover-traffic or a rendezvous beacon keyed by `z`.
identified.notes: Highest author count in the batch, but that count is inflated because every packet uses a new key. The crawl shape classifier labeled the content nip44, but the version byte is 0x01 and the header is cleartext. 4 events carried a `t` tag (none in the samples).

identified.name: Fact Op (FIPS peer link-quality rating)
identified.app_or_protocol: nostr-identity / nostr-social-memory fact ops (mmalmi), published by nostr-vpn nodes on the FIPS mesh
identified.what_it_is: Generic append-only 'fact operation' event (FACT_OP_KIND = 7368; addressable snapshots are 37368): the subject is a UUID in an ['i', <uuid>, 'subject'] tag, every other tag name is a predicate (type, schema, created_at, rater, subject, rating, min_rating, max_rating, scope, sample_count, window_end, reason, tag), and the referenced npubs and scope strings are repeated as extra 'i' tags so they can be filtered. Content is empty. All the observed traffic is type=rating, scope=fips.peer: each nostr-vpn/FIPS mesh node rates its direct peers 0-100 from measured link quality (the reason tag holds e.g. 'loss=0.006 delivery=1.000 etx=1.01 srtt_ms=840 goodput_bps=782') and republishes this every few seconds. nostr-vpn reads these to rank peers and paid exits ('best-rated').
identified.notes: The busiest unsupported kind (~120k/day, 535 authors). It is machine telemetry: one event per peer link per interval, signed by mesh nodes whose keys are also FIPS network addresses. No merged NIP or open NIP PR was found; the only definition is the Rust constant. It does not overlap with NIP-85 or NIP-32. Two samples carried NIP-44 content and 'p' tags (probably another fact type). For Amethyst it is mostly a relay-load and storage concern: don't render it, and maybe add a known-kind stub so the relay/store layer and the `amy` census can name it.

identified.name: Full Throttle rider level
identified.app_or_protocol: 'Full Throttle' motorcycle racing game (unidentified web/mobile game)
identified.what_it_is: Per-player progress/leaderboard record for a motorcycle racing game. Addressable with fixed d='full-throttle-level' and t='full-throttle-level-v1'; content JSON {v:1, name:'Rider####', mi:<miles ridden>, lv:<level>, c:<club?|null>}. Each player key keeps one latest record.
identified.notes: 234 authors, all throwaway-looking keys with auto names 'RiderNNNN'. Same authors publish kind 4277 (t='full-throttle-review-v1', in-game star rating with bike/map names like 'BMW M 1000 RR', 'Neon City', 'Dallas Freeway'). No public source/repo found; game identity is inferred from payloads only.

identified.name: PlanX node beacon
identified.what_it_is: Replaceable presence beacon. Single tag ['i','planx:<uuid-like node id starting 2001002a->'] (NIP-73-style external id). Content JSON {payload:{type:'beacon', msgId, from:<node id>, to:'all', timestamp(ms), data:{roles:['server','client'], generation, status?:'leave'}}, signature:<base64 64-byte sig>} — an app-level signature inside the Nostr event, i.e. the Nostr event is just a carrier for a mesh/overlay node announcement.
identified.notes: 214 authors. Node ids look like IPv6-prefix-derived identifiers (2001:002a…). No public source found; ignore.

identified.name: Population Census
identified.app_or_protocol: fount (AI character platform by steve02081504), NIP-F5 draft
identified.what_it_is: Probabilistic node census for P2P overlays. Each node publishes at most one event per time window with inclusion probability p, and readers use a Horvitz-Thompson estimator to estimate how many nodes are online. Tags are `t`=<network scope> ('fount') and `x`='census', with no `d` tag (addressable at d=''). In the wild the content is base64 of JSON {nodeHash,nodePubKey,ts,p,sig}, where the inner sig is the network's own node signature.
identified.notes: The NIP says content is plain JSON, but the observed events base64-wrap it. 4 events in the census have a `d` tag and NIP-44 content, which is unrelated reuse of the kind.

identified.name: fount P2P network advert
identified.what_it_is: Addressable discovery advert (`NOSTR_ADVERT_KIND = 30787`) for nodes of the fount AI-character platform's P2P layer. Tags are `t=fount`, `t=<rendezvous key hash>`, `x=advert` and `d=<rendezvous key>`, so many nodes share the same d/t values. The content is base64 of JSON `{iv, authTag, ciphertext}` (AES-GCM under a room secret) and holds node hash, relay pool and listen relays. The same library uses kind 20787 for ephemeral WebRTC signalling and kind 30789 for a census (`t=fount`, `x=census`).
identified.notes: Verified in the published npm package source: `export const NOSTR_ADVERT_KIND = 30787`. 170 authors.

identified.name: Unidentified encrypted blob with a random d-tag
identified.what_it_is: Regular kind, but with a 'd' tag holding 64 random hex chars. Content is a NIP-44 v2 payload (version byte 0x02) of fixed padded length (1284 or 1456 b64 chars), so the plaintext is roughly 0.9-1 KB. There is no 'p' tag, and 3 events carry an expiration. 111 of 140 authors published exactly once, which suggests throwaway or per-message keys. 22 of the 25 kind-1461 events share an exact created_at second with a 1460 from a different key, so the two kinds are published as a pair.
identified.notes: Searches for the kind number and on GitHub turned up no spec. The pattern (one-shot keys, a d-tag nonce, an encrypted payload with no recipient tag, a companion 1461 marker) looks like an anonymous mailbox/drop or sealed-envelope protocol in which the recipient finds the message by a precomputed d-tag. The 1461 d-tag is not sha256 of the 1460 id, pubkey or d-tag.

identified.name: Iris AppKeys roster snapshot / group roster
identified.what_it_is: Addressable 'fact' event discriminated by a `type` tag. type=app_keys_roster_snapshot (most events): the owner identity publishes the list of device/app keys authorized to act for it in double-ratchet messaging: d/i=<uuid> 'subject', owner_pubkey, one `device` tag per device pubkey with added-at timestamp, `p` per device, schema=1. type=group_roster: group membership for Iris sender-key groups (protocol=sender_key_v1) with group_id, name, admin/member tags, revision, created_by/at, updated_at. Content empty.
identified.notes: APP_KEYS_SNAPSHOT_KIND = 37368 in both TS and Rust. Relevant only if Amethyst wants interop with Iris double-ratchet DMs/multi-device; otherwise ignore. Group roster names seen like 'Sample group', 'Project Hello' (test traffic).

identified.name: Opaque p-tagged encrypted drop
identified.what_it_is: Regular event from a fresh throwaway pubkey (96 events / 96 authors) with a single p tag to a recipient and ~860–1150 bytes of base64 ciphertext that is NOT NIP-44 v2 (no 0x02 version byte; 4 of 96 are NIP-44). Some recipient p values are obviously synthetic ('cdcd…cd', 'aeeee…000000'). Looks like a sealed-sender / anonymous mailbox or app RPC addressed to a recipient key.
identified.notes: One-author-per-event pattern implies ephemeral keys. Nothing human-readable.

identified.name: Anonymate encrypted account state
identified.app_or_protocol: anonymate (unknown app; collides with Corny Chat 'Slide Set')
source_urls: https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/commit/1c166044 (Corny Chat 30388 registration, later removed from README in 861675be 'fix: sanity', May 2026)
identified.what_it_is: Per-user encrypted settings sync. `d`=`account-state-v1:<dataset>` (e.g. manualPeers, followedChannels), `app`=anonymate, `dataset`=<name>, `p`=self, and content is NIP-04 ciphertext (`?iv=`) encrypted to the author's own key. This is NIP-78-style private app data on a dedicated kind.
identified.notes: Kind 30388 was registered in the NIPs README as Corny Chat Slide Set until May 2026, and Ditto still labels it that way. The anonymate usage is a collision, so any parser must check the `app` tag. No public source for anonymate was found.

identified.name: Unidentified NIP-44 blob keyed by d-tag
identified.what_it_is: Regular (non-addressable) kind that still carries a single `d` tag holding a 64-hex value. The value is distinct per event and is not sha256(pubkey). The content is NIP-44 v2 ciphertext of a constant 388 base64 chars, so the plaintext is a small fixed-size record (at most about 224 bytes). There is no p tag, so it is most likely self-encrypted app state or a per-object secret.
identified.notes: 83 authors and 151 events. Using a d-tag on a regular kind suggests an app that believes it is replaceable or uses `d` as a lookup key.

identified.name: Posting Streak
identified.what_it_is: Replaceable event (one per user) with the author's self-reported posting streak: 'start' and 'end' unix-second tags plus alt 'Posting streak'; content is empty. The streak is live while now - end <= 36h, and days = max(1, ceil((end-start)/86400)). Only 'creative' kinds (notes, articles, media, polls, etc.) extend it. The author's client maintains it and repairs it from the author's own events. The kind number keypad-spells 1-FIRE.
identified.notes: A small profile badge ('🔥 12 days'). Trust-based, and it only affects the author's own profile. Ditto adds a 'published_at' tag too.

identified.name: Anonymate profile
identified.app_or_protocol: Anonymate (unidentified anonymous social app, Portuguese-speaking users)
identified.what_it_is: App-scoped profile record. Addressable with d=<username>, `u`=<username>, `app`='anonymate', and a `pfx` tag for every prefix of the username (2..n chars) so relays can do prefix/autocomplete search via #pfx filters. Content JSON {username, displayName, image, bannerImage, bio/about/description, activeProfileBadge, ts(ms)}; 2 events have NIP-44 content.
identified.notes: Same authors publish 30388 (d='account-state-v1:<dataset>', NIP-04-style '?iv=' encrypted app state), 34552 (action=join), 4551 (posts) and 30032, all tagged app=anonymate. No public source found. Effectively a parallel kind-0 inside one app; the 'pfx' prefix-index trick is notable.

identified.name: Event Paths (NIP-116 draft) / de-facto generic app data
identified.app_or_protocol: Multiple apps: COURA (alias→pubkey registry), persona-bubble-field (io.github.lokuyow), 'bro-order' service marketplace, einundzwanzig-meetup-app, PixelPocket presence, an encrypted folder/drive app
identified.what_it_is: Kind 30079 was proposed in open NIP-116 (mmalmi) as an event identified by a human-readable path in its d tag (e.g. 'user/profile/name') with JSON content and an f 'directory' tag; separately open NIP-79 Stories PR #2386 reuses 30079 for 'story highlights'. In the wild it is used like a second NIP-78 (30078) arbitrary-app-data bucket: COURA publishes d=alias ('NNA-X54-8HM') + content {alias,pubkey}; persona-bubble-field stores game state under d='io.github.lokuyow.persona-bubble-field:profile-state:<event id>'; einundzwanzig-meetup-app records organizer/attendee role per meetup; an unnamed app stores encrypted folders (tags encrypted/key/wk, content {name:'probe-…',encrypted:true}); NIP-44 blobs from others.
identified.notes: No single schema; 51 authors across ≥6 apps. Two conflicting open NIP PRs claim the number. Do not type it in Quartz beyond perhaps treating it like NIP-78 app data.

identified.name: Myria signed spend/settlement record
identified.what_it_is: Testnet traffic of an unidentified protocol. Tags are `t`=test-myria-discovery-v1, `g`=network id hash, `o`=object/offer id, `s`=record hash. Content is `MYRS1:` plus base64url CBOR (magic 'MYR\x01') holding transactions, fee-market profiles, spend intents, witness signatures and receipt chains. Sibling kinds 9420 (`MYRD1:` discovery) and 9424 (`MYRM1:`) carry the same tag family.
identified.notes: Each event has a fresh author (50 events, 50 authors), and the network is self-labelled 'test'. No public source was found.

identified.name: Myria discovery record (test)
identified.what_it_is: Discovery or announcement records tagged `t=test-myria-discovery-v1`. They have a `g` tag (64-hex group or namespace id shared by all events), an `s` tag (64-hex service id), and an optional `o` tag (owner) plus many `a` tags (64-hex, not NIP-01 coordinates). The content is `MYRD1:` followed by base64url CBOR that embeds the same hashes and catbox.moe .html URLs.
identified.notes: The name is explicitly a test (46 one-shot authors). The `a` tag is reused for raw hashes, so Amethyst's address parser would reject it. No public repository found.

identified.name: Page view counter update
identified.what_it_is: Regular event that a website's visitors publish to bump a shared page-view counter: 'd' = page id (e.g. com.citadelwire.page-views.home), 'u' = page URL, 't' view-count/citadel-wire, and an alt. Content is the new count as a plain integer string, which the client computes as the latest seen + 1.
identified.notes: 41 authors because each visitor signs one, often with ad-hoc keys. A regular kind with a d tag means relays keep every increment. Not useful to Amethyst.

identified.name: 'fidelity' UTXO outpoint claim
identified.what_it_is: Addressable with d='fidelity:<txid>:<vout>' and content '<txid>:<vout>' (a Bitcoin outpoint), plus NIP-40 expiration 24h after creation. Each of 40 authors publishes one; the same few outpoints are announced by several different keys.
identified.notes: Looks like a JoinMarket-style 'fidelity bond' or UTXO-backed anti-sybil advertisement refreshed daily, but no proof/signature is in the event and no source code was found for kind 37778. Unidentified.

identified.name: Biosenger presence / relay list
identified.what_it_is: Addressable, d='biosenger-presence', app='biosenger', empty content. Tags: ['relay', <connected>, <total>] counters and one 'relay-urls' tag listing the app's relay URLs (data-space.world relays, digitalforlifeagency workers.dev relays, plus public ones). Acts as an online-presence heartbeat + relay advertisement for the Biosenger messenger.
identified.notes: Same authors also publish 30215/30218/30225-30228 'infinity-*' kinds (see 30218, 30226), so it is one app family squatting a block of 302xx kinds. No public spec found.

identified.name: 'fidelity' outpoint announcement
source_urls: https://mempool.space/api/tx/<txid> (txids not found on Bitcoin mainnet)
identified.what_it_is: Short-lived addressable events with `d`=`fidelity:<txid>:<vout>`, content equal to the same `<txid>:<vout>`, and `expiration` 24h out. In the samples only 5 distinct outpoints appear, each published by 4 different pubkeys. Sibling kind 37778 has the identical shape.
identified.notes: Reads like a JoinMarket-style fidelity-bond / UTXO-ownership advert, but the txids are not on Bitcoin mainnet (they may be testnet/signet or another chain), and no spec or repo was found.

identified.name: Unidentified p-tagged NIP-44 message
identified.what_it_is: Each event has exactly one `p` tag and NIP-44 v2 content. In half the samples the p tag is the author (self-encrypted state) and in the rest it is another user. Ciphertext lengths cluster at 176, 220 and 944 chars, i.e. a few fixed message types. Possibly an app's encrypted sync or RPC between a user's own devices and peers.
identified.notes: 31 authors and 142 events. The kind number may be chosen to sit next to NIP-23's 30023 but has no visible relation to it.

identified.name: MLS KeyPackage (Keychat legacy NIP-EE style)
identified.what_it_is: Replaceable event whose content is a hex-encoded MLS KeyPackage, published so others can invite the user to MLS large groups. Tags: mls_protocol_version '1.0', ciphersuite '1', extensions 'RequiredCapabilities,LastResort,RatchetTree,Unknown(62003)', relay list, client 'Keychat'. This is Keychat's pre-Marmot (NIP-EE era) key package kind, paired with Welcome kind 444.
identified.notes: Quartz implements Marmot MIP-00 KeyPackages as addressable kind 30443 (+ 10051 relay list). Keychat still publishes replaceable 10443, so Amethyst can't find Keychat users' key packages. Keychat's KeyPackages require extension 0xF233 (Unknown(62003), the old NIP-EE group-data id), but Quartz's Marmot uses marmot_group_data 0xF2EE. A legacy reader alone therefore won't give working Marmot<->Keychat group interop. One sample from client 'meiso' instead holds a Signal-style JSON prekey bundle (identityKey/signedPrekey/oneTimePrekey), so the kind is also squatted for Signal X3DH bundles.

identified.name: Mostro instance info
identified.what_it_is: Addressable info/status event of a Mostro P2P-exchange daemon (d=<mostro pubkey>, z='info', y=['mostro', <instance name>]). Tags carry config: mostro_version/commit, min/max order amount, fee, pow, pow_first_contact, protocol_version, expiration windows, fiat_currencies_accepted, LND node version/pubkey/alias/uris/network, bond_* anti-abuse settings, maintenance_mode. Content empty.
identified.notes: Part of Mostro's split of its old single kind 38383 into 38383 orders / 38384 ratings / 38385 info / 38386 disputes. Quartz already has nip69P2pOrderEvents (38383); 38385 lets a P2P-order UI show which instance (fees, limits, currencies) published an order. Instance keys mined with leading zeros (PoW vanity).

identified.name: SMJ prediction-market bet/position
identified.what_it_is: Addressable bet record, d=64-hex position id. Heavily duplicated tags: market/m (market id), network/n ('demo'), status/s ('confirmed'), outcome/o (YES/NO/…), amount, price, side/x ('buy'), rail ('lightning'), fee, payout_address [id,'lnbits'], t 'smj-bet', smj 'true', NIP-32 labels L 'agent' / l 'ai'. Content JSON {amount, avgPrice, outcomeId, trader, rail, traderName, feeSats, feePercent, feeCurrency}. Sibling kind 38023 ('smj-pool') carries per-market pool totals.
identified.notes: 22,501 events from only 25 authors on network 'demo' with trader names like 'Bob5 Ecash' and L/l 'ai agent' labels — bot-generated test traffic flooding relays. No public spec found.

identified.name: Sealed mailbox message (unidentified)
identified.what_it_is: Regular event with `s`=<32-byte hex routing tag> and `expiration`=+7 days. Content is base64 binary of fixed size (~1.6 KB, so padded): 0x03||33-byte compressed ephemeral secp256k1 pubkey, 32-byte salt/nonce, u32 inner kind (=3560), u32 0, then ciphertext. Authors are throwaway keys.
identified.notes: This is a custom envelope, not NIP-44. Its shape matches a sealed-sender / stealth-address mailbox where `s` is a recipient-derived lookup tag.

identified.name: RoboSats coordinator rating
identified.what_it_is: Addressable review of a RoboSats coordinator after a trade, published by the robot's key. `d=<coordinator shortAlias>:<orderId>` (lake, temple, freeport, bazaar, ...), `p=<coordinator pubkey>`, `rating=<0..1>` (stars/5), and `sig=<coordinator-signed token>` from `POST /api/review/` that proves the reviewer actually traded, which clients schnorr-verify. The content is empty.
identified.notes: RoboSats coordinators sync kinds 38383, 31986 and 1059 between relays. Quartz already has NIP-69 kind 38383, so these ratings could feed coordinator reputation in an order view.

identified.name: Unidentified companion marker to kind 1460
identified.what_it_is: Regular kind with only a 'd' tag (64 random hex chars) and plaintext content '{"v":1}'. Each one is signed by a throwaway key, and 22 of 25 share an exact created_at with a kind-1460 encrypted blob signed by a different key. Looks like a version/ack/announce marker in the same unknown drop protocol as 1460.
identified.notes: See 1460. No link to 1460 found in the tag values themselves (tested id, pubkey and d, raw and sha256).

identified.name: P2P swarm peer announce
identified.app_or_protocol: unidentified (topic-hash rendezvous; peer ids look like iroh-style 32-byte base32 node ids)
identified.what_it_is: Regular event, single r tag = 64-hex topic/room hash. Content JSON {from:<52-char lowercase base32 peer id>, to:null, kind:'announce', peer_id, caps:['ptag']}. Used as a relay-based bootstrap/discovery channel where peers announce themselves on a topic so others can connect directly.
identified.notes: 77 events / 23 authors; most announce on one topic hash. Peer-id encoding (RFC4648 base32, 52 chars) matches 32-byte keys like iroh node ids, but no source confirms.

identified.name: Bitflash node descriptor
identified.what_it_is: Peer-discovery record for a Bitflash full node. Addressable with d='btf-descriptor-2' (or '-testnet'); content JSON {v:3, pubkey, onion:'<v3>.onion:8433', enc:<encryption key>, meeting_node, created, sig, sig3} — a self-certifying descriptor signed by the key the node's .btf address derives from. Republished frequently.
identified.notes: 23 nodes, 351 events. Kind 38503 (same authors) appears to be the pool announcement. Pure infrastructure for a separate altcoin's P2P layer.

identified.name: Full Throttle game review
identified.what_it_is: Public in-game review. `t`=full-throttle-review-v1, and the content is JSON {v,rating,text,name ('Rider1234'),bike,map ('Neon City','Dallas Freeway'),device,rides,mins,when}. Each review is signed by a throwaway key.
identified.notes: The data is self-describing, but no repo or site was found. These are app telemetry/feedback, not social posts.

identified.name: Unidentified shared-namespace blob (ns2v5/ns2v7)
identified.what_it_is: Addressable events whose `d` tag is a shared namespace id (`ns2v5_d4051f6c4130b037`, `ns2v7_aadbaddff9b290c6`) used by many unrelated authors. Each carries an `expiration` 1 h out. The content is about 948 chars of raw base64 (not NIP-44 framed), presumably symmetric ciphertext under a namespace key. It behaves like a per-user presence or state slot within a versioned shared room.
identified.notes: 22 authors with 1 event each.

identified.name: Lana digital-being liveness heartbeat
identified.what_it_is: Addressable, d='heartbeat', t tags 'lana-kyc','liveness','public', status 'alive'. Content JSON {schema:'lana-being-heartbeat-v1', being_pubkey, being_name, being_domain (<name>.lana.is), status, adoptee_count, alive_at}. Each 'being' (AI persona with its own key and subdomain) republishes it to prove it is alive; sibling kind 39020 'lana-being-commons' is the being's public profile/presence.
identified.notes: 21 authors, all bots of one service. No public spec found.

identified.name: Lana Being Commons presence card
identified.what_it_is: Self-published presence/profile card for AI 'digital beings' hosted under *.lana.is. `d`=`presence:<pubkey>`, `protocol`=lana-being-commons 1.0.0, `p`=self, `name`, `domain`, and `t`=being-commons/digital-being/lana. Content is JSON {protocol,version,name,summary,domain,language,interests,capabilities,communication_policy{public_topics,dm_invites,rate limits},updated_at}.
identified.notes: This is an agent directory for an AI-persona network (mostly Slovenian). It is self-describing and no external spec was found.

identified.name: Myria discovery / mesh message (unidentified)
identified.what_it_is: Two shapes. (1) 20 events tagged t='test-myria-discovery-v1' with hex 'g' (group/network id), 'o' (origin pubkey-like) and 'm' (message hash) tags. Content is 'MYRM1:' + base64url CBOR starting with the magic 'MYR\x01', holding hash-addressed records, apparently a peer/peer-record discovery beacon. (2) 8 events with only an 'r' hex tag and short opaque base64 content, likely encrypted payloads in the same system.
identified.notes: No public source for 'myria'/'MYRM1' found on GitHub or the web. The 't' value says test/v1, so it's an experiment.

identified.name: unidentified opaque blob
identified.what_it_is: Regular event with only a NIP-40 expiration tag (exactly 14 days). Content is standard base64 of a binary blob of fixed sizes (1052 or 4124 bytes) that is not NIP-44 (first byte varies) — looks like fixed-size cells/ciphertext. Many distinct fresh keys post at the same second.
identified.notes: Fixed cell sizes + throwaway keys + synchronized timestamps suggest a mixnet/dead-drop or anonymous mailbox system using one-shot keys. No source found.

identified.name: Marmot KeyPackage (legacy, non-addressable)
identified.app_or_protocol: Marmot / MLS over Nostr (MDK = White Noise's Marmot Development Kit; also rizq, EpochShield)
identified.what_it_is: Legacy MIP-00 KeyPackage that predates the addressable kind 30443. Tags are `mls_protocol_version`, `mls_ciphersuite`, `mls_extensions`, `mls_proposals`, `relays`, `i` (KeyPackageRef), `encoding=base64` and `client`. The content is a base64 MLS KeyPackage, not NIP-44: it starts `00 01 00 01`, i.e. a bare KeyPackage without the MLSMessage envelope. Quartz has no typed class because it treats 443 only as a migration alias: `KeyPackageUtils.LEGACY_KIND = 443`, `isKeyPackageKind()`, and `MarmotFilters.keyPackagesMigration()` query [30443, 443]. EventFactory has no 443 branch, so these events parse as generic `Event`.
identified.suggested_quartz_package: marmot/mip00KeyPackages/ (could map 443 to KeyPackageEvent-like reader or keep as legacy alias)
identified.notes: MDK/0.8.0 (18 of 26 events) still publishes kind 443, so in the wild legacy 443 dominates. `MarmotFilters.keyPackagesMigration()` has no callers, so Amethyst may never fetch these and cannot invite White Noise users who only have 443 KeyPackages. Bare (unframed) bytes are accepted by `KeyPackageUtils.decodeKeyPackage`. rizq publishes 443 with empty content and non-standard `ciphersuite`/`extensions` tag names (named extensions like `nostr_group_data`), which is non-conformant.

identified.name: Word5 game score
identified.what_it_is: Regular event recording a daily Wordle-like result. Tags: game=word5, schema=word5.score.v1, puzzle number, result (guess count or X), difficulty, streak, maxStreak, played, won, version, source URL, t word5/gaming. Content is the same data as JSON (game, puzzle, result, hardMode, streak, maxStreak, played, won, version). The app's server builds leaderboards from these.
identified.notes: Kind 5555 lies inside the NIP-90 DVM job-request range (5000-5999), so DVM-aware clients and relays may treat these as job requests. It could render as a small score card ('WORD5 #734 4/6'), but it's niche. The same app also posts kind-1 notes with the same schema tag.

identified.name: UPlanet Cookie Vault manifest / klatsch push registration (kind collision)
identified.app_or_protocol: UPlanet / Astroport.ONE ('NIP-101 Cookie Vault'); separately an unidentified 'Klatsch' app
identified.what_it_is: Two unrelated uses. (a) UPlanet/Astroport.ONE: d='cookies', t=['cookies','uplanet'], content JSON manifest mapping domain -> IPFS CID of a NaCl-encrypted browser cookie blob, plus '_bro_commands' (scraper config/last_check), republished on each write. (b) 13 events with t='klatsch-push-v1', d=<random 32-hex>, NIP-44 content — apparently push-notification registrations of an unidentified 'Klatsch' messenger.
identified.notes: Collision between two apps. Cookie Vault manifests are in cleartext JSON (domains only, cookies themselves encrypted on IPFS).

identified.name: Encrypted blob + WebRTC call signalling (mixed)
identified.what_it_is: Two uses: (a) ~75% of samples: no tags, content is a JSON array of two byte arrays '[[16 IV bytes],[ciphertext bytes]]' — AES-style ciphertext serialized as number arrays, i.e. an app's private encrypted storage/messages; (b) plaintext WebRTC signalling between two keys: p tag to the peer and content {type:'candidate'|'hangup'|offer/answer, data:{candidate,sdpMid,sdpMLineIndex}}, leaking ICE candidates (IPv6 addresses) in the clear.
identified.notes: 814 events / 17 authors. Kind 1000 is just the first number of the regular range, so it is a popular 'default' pick for ad-hoc apps.

identified.name: DEN Chat server membership / key envelope
identified.what_it_is: Part of the DEN Chat family: 36942 is the server definition (roles and permissions JSON, relays, blossom servers), 36943 is a channel message (`h`=server UUID, `c`=channel UUID, `epoch`, client 'DEN Chat'), and 36946 is server status. A 36944 has `d`=server UUID (or the member's own pubkey with `a`=36942 coordinate + `version` 2) and NIP-44 content (or empty when cleared/`deleted`). All carry a NIP-13 `nonce` PoW (difficulty 15).
identified.notes: Probably a per-member, per-server encrypted record (membership or group-key share). The family was identified from sibling kinds in the census, and no public repo was found.

identified.name: Infinity Builder private profile
identified.what_it_is: Addressable per-user settings/profile document with `d=infinity-builder-profile` and `visibility=private`. The content is `enc1:` followed by NIP-44 v2 ciphertext (self-encrypted). It is app-private profile or state storage, similar in shape to NIP-78 app data.
identified.notes: The app is identified only from the d-tag. 16 authors. The `enc1:` prefix is an app convention that marks the format of the encrypted payload.

identified.name: Kilojoin coinjoin pool
identified.what_it_is: Addressable coinjoin-pool announcement modelled on Joinstr (whose pool kind is 2022): d = pool id, t='kilojoin', network='blake2b'. JSON content holds v, app 'kilowallet', network, id, public_key, denomination, fee_rate, min_peers, max_peers, private, timeout and state (open/aborted/...), plus the current peer count. Peers join over the relay, and no coordinator holds funds.
identified.notes: Not Bitcoin: it's for a BLAKE2b-based chain.

identified.name: Communikey community definition
identified.what_it_is: Replaceable event that turns any keypair into a community: the community pubkey is the identifier. Tags list community relays (`r`), blossom servers, and named content sections: each `content` tag names a section (Calendar, Chat, Articles, Forum, Wikis, Learning, Polls, Social Bookmarks...) followed by `k` tags for the kinds it accepts and an `access` (e.g. members) rule; edufeed adds `membership` (id + membership service URL) and `strict`. Posts target the community with an `h` tag.
identified.notes: Unmerged community spec in active use by edufeed.org (German OER platform) and Flotilla-Budabit. 14 authors seen, all on relay.edufeed.org. Worth tracking as a third community model next to NIP-72 and NIP-29.

identified.name: YalaChat / 'israel-network' login ping + SOS e2ee messages
identified.what_it_is: Regular events with t tags. Most are login pings: t 'login' + 'israel-network', content {type:'login', at:<ISO time>}. Others carry encrypted payloads: p tag + t 'yalachat' with content {family:'sos-e2ee', v:1, alg:'nip44', ct:<NIP-44 ciphertext>}, or p tag + t <32-hex room id> with opaque base64. Sibling kinds 1051/1054 (sos-global-identity) and 33051 (sos_trivia_v1 presence) come from the same authors.
identified.notes: 13 authors. Login pings publicly leak per-user activity timestamps. No public spec found.

identified.name: OuroSwap escrow message
identified.what_it_is: Regular event with `t`=`ouroswap:<escrow contract address>` (or `ouroswap:accept:<hash>`) and `client`=ouroswap. Content is JSON {id,escrow,from (EVM address),createdAt,ciphertext (0x-hex ECIES-style blob)}. It is an encrypted coordination message between swap counterparties, using Nostr as a bulletin board.
identified.notes: All samples have the same `from` EVM address. No public source was found.

identified.name: Group-scoped encrypted blob (y-tag)
identified.what_it_is: Regular event from one-shot pubkeys, tags ['y', <32-hex group/room id>] and NIP-40 expiration (~6–7 days). Content is base64url ciphertext (not NIP-44; random-looking from byte 0) ranging 300 B to ~37 KB. Looks like an anonymous group/room message bus or file transfer keyed by a shared room id.
identified.notes: 12 events / 12 authors, 2 room ids.

identified.name: r-tagged opaque blob (unidentified)
identified.what_it_is: Regular event with a single `r`=<32-byte hex room/rendezvous id> and base64 ciphertext content (~70-100 bytes, no NIP-44 version byte). Several throwaway authors post to the same `r`. Sibling kinds 9423 and 9424 (r-tagged variants) have the same shape.
identified.notes: This looks like an anonymous shared-key group channel (room id = hash, symmetric encryption). The tag is not a NIP-01 URL `r`.

identified.name: DEN Chat encrypted channel message
identified.app_or_protocol: DEN Chat (client tag); no public spec found
identified.what_it_is: Addressable (one d=UUID per message) encrypted group-chat message. `h=<group UUID>`, `c=<channel UUID>`, `epoch=<key epoch>`, `published_at`, `client=DEN Chat`, and a NIP-13 `nonce` at difficulty 15. Replies use NIP-01 `a` tags pointing at other 36943 messages with root/reply markers. The content is raw base64 symmetric ciphertext (key per group epoch), and `emoji`/`sticker` tags also carry encrypted values.
identified.notes: 135 events from 12 authors. Making each message addressable lets messages be edited in place. Unrelated to the 2023 denostr-lab/denny project as far as can be told.

identified.name: Unidentified replaceable 'v' list (UUID + relay + index)
identified.what_it_is: Replaceable event whose tags are ['v', <uuid>, <relay-url>, <small integer index>] entries (1-3 per event). Content is empty (11) or NIP-44 (3). It looks like a per-user pointer list: UUID-identified items (vaults? votes? sessions?) and the relay each one lives on, with an ordinal. The same UUID shows up across users (e.g. 8a53bdbe... on wss://nostr.mom).
identified.notes: No source found for the kind number. 12 authors.

identified.name: SNS envelope? / encrypted key blob (contested)
identified.app_or_protocol: Possibly NIP-SNS Shared Note Storage (damus notedeck draft) or an app storing encrypted nsecs
identified.what_it_is: Regular event with no tags and NIP-44 v2 content, authored by an otherwise unused key — same shape as a PNS (1080) note. notedeck's NIP-SNS draft names 1081 the 'SNS envelope' (outer wrapper signed by a key derived from a shared team_root, carrying a kind-13 seal). But every observed event is exactly 163 bytes of ciphertext (<=96 bytes plaintext), too small to hold a signed seal.
identified.notes: In the PNS PR thread, a commenter (sh1ftred) says they want to use 1081 to store encrypted nsecs; a ~64-96 byte plaintext fits that better. So the live traffic is probably not SNS.

identified.name: Blobbi virtual pet
identified.what_it_is: Addressable Tamagotchi-style pet whose whole state lives in tags. `d=blobbi-<pubkey12>-<petId10>`, `b=blobbi:ecosystem:v1`, `name`, `seed`, `stage` (egg/baby/adult), `state`, stats (`hunger`, `happiness`, `health`, `hygiene`, `energy`), appearance (`base_color`, `secondary_color`, `eye_color`, `pattern`, `special_mark`, `size`), progression, care streak and `client=Ditto` with a 31990 handler. The content is JSON progression quests (`{evolution:[...]}`) or a short text description.
identified.notes: Public, with a `visible_to_others` tag, and republished on every interaction (42 events from 11 authors). It could be shown as a profile card using the alt/content text or NIP-89 handoff to Ditto. Low priority.

identified.name: Blobbonaut Profile (Blobbi virtual pet)
identified.what_it_is: Replaceable owner profile for the Blobbi virtual-pet game: d='blobbonaut-<pubkey prefix>', b='blobbi:ecosystem:v1', name, 'has' tags pointing at owned Blobbis (the pets are kind 31124 addressable states), pettingLevel, xp/coins/level, blobbi_onboarding_done, current_companion. Content is JSON with missions and room_furniture/room_layouts. Related kinds: 14919 interaction, 14920 breeding, 14921 lifecycle record, 31124 pet state, 1124 social interaction.
identified.suggested_quartz_package: blobbi/ (only if the pet game is wanted)
identified.notes: Game-save data. If anything is rendered, it would be the 31124 pet, not this profile.

identified.name: Fedi FMan advertisement
identified.what_it_is: Addressable ad (d='fman-ad', t='fedi-fman') by an FMan (federation-manager) service so people setting up a Fedimint federation can find guardian hosting. Content JSON {payload:{version, fman_id_pubkey, service_pubkey, issued_at, expires_at(~1h), api_endpoints:[{transport:'iroh', url}], availability{fedimintd_version, federation_sizes}, plans[{InfiniteBestEffort:{price_msats}}], holder_authorizations[...]}, proof:{signature}}; the signature is over SHA256('fedi-fman-advertisement/v1\0'||JCS(payload)).
identified.notes: Same spec reserves 37702-37708 (FLIP provider ad, attester issuer authority, credential revocation, holder authorization, encrypted backups, setup-payment federations). Tags are only indexing hints; verifiers must check the signed payload.

identified.name: Infinity encrypted local-state backup
identified.what_it_is: Addressable, d='infinity-local-state', visibility 'private', optional backup 'blossom'. Content is 'enc1:' + NIP-44 v2 ciphertext (self-encrypted) of the app's local state, up to ~38 KB; when backup=blossom the payload is small (state stored on Blossom, event holds the pointer).
identified.notes: Same author set as 30085 and 30226; part of a 302xx block (30215 'infinity-builder-profile', 30225-30228…).

identified.name: Routstr provider analytics snapshot
identified.what_it_is: ANALYTICS_KIND = 38422 in routstr-core, enabled by default. Each node publishes one replaceable usage snapshot with `d`=`<provider_id>:stats`, `provider`=<id>, `schema`=routstr.analytics.snapshot.v1. Content is JSON with endpoint_urls (clearnet + onion), windows, model_usage_mix (per-model counts, tokens, revenue msats), top models and summary. It feeds routstr.com/stats.
identified.notes: This is the companion to the NIP-91 provider listing kind 38421 (Routstr). It is only relevant if Amethyst ever lists AI providers.

identified.name: NIP-4E encryption-key transfer request
identified.app_or_protocol: NIP-4E decoupled encryption keys (draft); implemented by psstpsst (CodyTseng)
identified.what_it_is: Signed by the identity key from a new device that lacks the decoupled encryption private key. It has empty content, `P=<requester client pubkey>` and an equal compatibility alias `pubkey=<same>`, plus optional `relay` and `n` (wanted encryption pubkey). Existing devices compare a pairing code out of band and answer with kind 4455: the encryption privkey NIP-44-encrypted from a sender client key to the requester client key. The requester accepts it only if it matches the `n` tag of the identity's kind 10044.
identified.suggested_quartz_package: experimental/decoupling/ (next to EncryptionKeyListEvent 10044; add 4454 request + 4455 transfer)
identified.notes: Quartz already implements kind 10044 (`EncryptionKeyListEvent`) but not the 4454/4455 multi-device handshake, which is the piece needed to use decoupled keys on a second device. 10 authors.

identified.name: Active Profile Theme
identified.what_it_is: Replaceable event (one per user) holding the user's active profile theme: 'c' color tags (hex, role background/text/primary), 'f' font tags (family, woff2 URL, role body/title), optional 'bg' background image (imeta-style url/mode/m), 'title', and 'a'/'p' credit tags when the theme was adopted from a kind-36767 Theme Definition or another user. Content is empty, alt 'Active profile theme'. Clients fetch {kinds:[16767],authors:[pk],limit:1} when showing a profile.
identified.notes: Already mentioned in Amethyst's commons/feeds/RepostRenderability.kt as a known untyped kind. Used by 3 clients. Could theme profile pages, or at least render the 36767 definitions as shareable theme cards.

identified.name: Anonymate post marker (like/bookmark?)
identified.what_it_is: Addressable event with no d tag (so one per author), tags app='anonymate', e=<post id>, p=<post author>, k='30023'. Empty content. The referenced e is an Anonymate kind-4551 post, despite k=30023.
identified.notes: Probably a 'current/last liked/pinned post' marker; since there is no d tag, each new one replaces the previous one. Same author set as 30310/30388/34552.

identified.name: Chunked encrypted file transfer
identified.what_it_is: Regular event from one-shot pubkeys with x <32-hex transfer id>, c <chunk index> and NIP-40 expiration (~2 weeks). Content is ~58 KB base64 (44,028 bytes decoded) of opaque ciphertext — fixed-size chunks of an encrypted file streamed through relays.
identified.notes: 198 events / 9 authors in stats; uses relays as blob storage.

identified.name: r-tagged opaque blob (unidentified)
identified.what_it_is: Same shape as 9422: `r`=<32-byte hex> plus ~100-byte base64 ciphertext, posted by many throwaway authors to the same r value.

identified.name: Grab-bag regular kind (encrypted room msgs, NIP-44 DMs, BetPod notice, Divine 'more like this')
identified.app_or_protocol: Multiple: unknown encrypted-room app, BetPod prediction markets, Divine (divine.video)
identified.what_it_is: No single schema. (a) Most events: t <64-hex room hash> + opaque base64 ciphertext (encrypted group chat keyed by room hash); (b) p tag + NIP-44 v2 ciphertext (DM-like); (c) BetPod: d=<market uuid>, market-status 'voided', market-resolves-at, market-version, t prediction/wager/betpod, alt text, plain content 'This market was voided…'; (d) Divine client: ['direction','more'] + e/a/p/k=34236 pointing at a Divine video + its hashtags, empty content — a 'show me more like this' recommendation-feedback signal.
identified.notes: 131 events / 8 authors. 4242 is a vanity number several apps picked independently; no spec found for any use. The Divine 'direction' signal is the only one an Amethyst video feed might care about.

identified.name: Blobbi social interaction
identified.what_it_is: Immutable interaction log for a Blobbi pet (kind 31124 is the pet's addressable state). Tags are `a`=31124:<owner>:<blobbi-d>, `p`=owner, `action` (feed|play|clean|medicate|boost), `source` (blobbi-page|companion), `blobbi`=short id, `item`=shop item, `alt` and `client`. Content is empty. The owner's client folds pending interactions into the 31124 state.
identified.notes: Only 8 authors (Ditto users). It could render as a small 'X fed Blobbi' activity line via `alt`, but the owning spec is the nostr-pet NIP-BB.

identified.name: Napstr audio catalogue entry (+ BetPod oracle node registration collision)
identified.what_it_is: Napstr is a P2P music-sharing app. Each kind 30421 entry is one shared audio file: `d`=`x`=sha256 file id, `t=napstr` plus up to 20 search-word `t` tags, `name`, `size`, `m` (audio MIME), `alt`. The content is JSON `{protocol:'napstr/1', fileId, filename, title, artist, album, format, mime, size, license, description, tags}`. A withdrawal replaces the entry with `{deleted:true}`; 1392 of 1646 events are withdrawals. Related kinds: 30422 (10-min seeding heartbeat) and 30423 (audiobook manifest), with negotiation over NIP-17/59. Separately, 13 events from betpod-oracle-poc reuse 30421 with `d=betpod-oracle-node:v1` to register AI-oracle nodes (ollama model, roles, FROST signer, stake).
identified.notes: This is a public catalogue, but it is useless without Napstr's P2P transfer. Kind collision between two unrelated apps. 8 authors produce 1646 events, so it is noisy for search indexes.

identified.name: Append-only list Add (nostr-mail senders list)
identified.what_it_is: An "Add" entry in an append-only list (kind 1991 = Remove). Only `d=nostr-mail/senders` was seen: the nostr-mail client's allow/block verdicts per sender (pubkey or pubkey+email for bridged mail). The `sender` entries live only inside NIP-44 encrypted content and are published to the user's NIP-65 write relays. Regular events accumulate instead of replacing a whole NIP-51 list.
identified.notes: The same project uses kind 1301 for email. The Append-Only Lists NIP is referenced by name only; no PR was found in nostr-protocol/nips. It could become protocol-infra if that NIP is proposed generally.

identified.name: Mostro user rating (collides with Paygress provider heartbeat)
identified.what_it_is: Mostro: addressable reputation snapshot signed by a Mostro daemon. d = the rated user's (trade) pubkey hex, z='rating', and tags total_reviews, total_rating (average), last_rating, max_rate, min_rate, days/since, plus a NIP-40 expiration (90 days by default). Content is empty. It is part of Mostro's 38383 orders / 38384 ratings / 38385 info / 38386 disputes / 38387 announcements family. Paygress (a Cashu-paid compute marketplace) reuses 38384 for provider heartbeats: d='paygress:heartbeat:v1:<npub>:<minute bucket>', t='paygress-heartbeat', JSON content with available_capacity and active_workloads.
identified.notes: Quartz already has P2POrderEvent (38383, NIP-69). Mostro's rating, info and dispute kinds sit beside it, and rating snapshots could be shown on a P2P order card ('4.9★ from 157 trades'). Paygress also uses 38383 for its compute offers, so P2POrderEvent parsing must tolerate non-Mostro 38383s. 98 of the sampled 448 events were Mostro ratings and 350 were Paygress heartbeats.

identified.name: Unidentified paired encrypted exchange (v1, o/f/i tags)
identified.what_it_is: Regular event: v='v1', 'o' and 'f' hex pubkeys (in the reply the two values are swapped, so likely 'own/self' and 'from/peer'), an 'i' UUID session id, and base64 content whose first byte is 0x01 (a NIP-44-v1-style or custom AEAD payload, not v2). Events come in request/response pairs a few seconds apart between two keys sharing the same 'i'. Looks like an app's encrypted 1:1 session or handshake channel.
identified.notes: Kind 1002 sits next to NIP-11-adjacent numbers but has nothing to do with them. Source not found.

identified.name: Napstr seeder availability
identified.app_or_protocol: Napstr (lnbits/napstr) — P2P music/file sharing over Tor
identified.what_it_is: Addressable heartbeat listing file IDs the author can seed right now. d='availability-NNNN' (groups of <=400 IDs) or 'availability-delta-<uuid>-NNNN', t='napstr-availability', expiration 10 minutes, republished every 4 minutes; content is a JSON array of lowercase SHA-256 file IDs. Consumers join it with the 30421 catalogue to find live seeders.
identified.notes: Part of Napstr: 30421 catalogue entries, 30422 availability, 30423 audiobook collections, NIP-17 for download negotiation, NIP-C7 kind 9 trollbox. 280 events from 8 authors (high churn because of the 4-min heartbeat).

identified.name: Kanban board (NIP PR #1665) / WalletScrutiny build verification (collision)
identified.app_or_protocol: Kanbanstr (kanban boards); WalletScrutiny.com reproducible-build verifications; an encrypted day-planner app
identified.what_it_is: Three users: (1) Kanbanstr board definition per open NIP PR #1665: d, title, description, col ['col',id,name,order], p maintainers; cards are kind 30302 with s/rank/a→30301. (2) WalletScrutiny build-verification results: d '<appId>:<version>:<platform>:<sha256>', i <appId>, version, platform, status (reproducible|not_reproducible|ftbfs), x <binary sha256, filename>, file-attachment/output-file (terminal recording hashes), based-on, client WalletScrutiny.com; content JSON {description, content:<markdown report>}. (3) A planner app storing per-day tasks: b <board hash>, col 'day', status open/deleted/done, d like 'fasting-reminder:2026-11-02', NIP-44 content.
identified.notes: Board events (kanban) and WalletScrutiny reproducibility reports are both human-meaningful. WalletScrutiny status is real security-relevant info (render-worthy as an app/release attestation, could pair with zapstore/NIP-82 app events). Kind collision means any typed parser must disambiguate by tags (title+col → board; i+status+x → verification).

identified.name: Infinity avatar photo pointer
identified.what_it_is: Addressable, d=<user pubkey hex>, visibility 'public', t 'infinity-avatar-photo', NIP-40 expiration. Content JSON {cid:<IPFS CIDv1 bafkrei…>, mime:'image/png', auto:true} or {off:true}. Points the app's avatar to an IPFS-hosted image.
identified.notes: Same authors as 30085/30218. Could in theory be a profile-picture source, but it's app-scoped and expiring.

identified.name: CI coordinator repository status
identified.app_or_protocol: Nostr CI / ngit-ci (NIP-C1, CI extension to NIP-34)
identified.what_it_is: A CI coordinator advertises that it is acting for a NIP-34 repository. `d` and `a`=30617 repo coordinate(s), `s`=acting, `W`=runner family (act|nix), `workflow-path` globs (.ngit/act/workflows/*.yml), `R`=runner selectors, `secret`=secret names only (never values), and `expiration` within 24h. Content is empty. Same family: 19843 coordinator advert (software 'ngit-ci'), 19844 readiness list, 9840 manual trigger, 9841 job result, 9842 workflow result, 9843/9844 service request/stop, 39842 workflow progress, 29846 secret update.
identified.notes: Relevant if Amethyst's NIP-34 git screens want to show CI status. 9842 (workflow result) and 39842 (progress) are the render-worthy ones, and 39844 tells you which coordinator serves a repo. The spec is also published on nostrhub.io.

identified.name: Infinity avatar personality profile
identified.what_it_is: `d`=author pubkey, `t`=infinity-avatar-personnalite, `visibility`=public, and a short `expiration`. Content is JSON personality sliders {v,aventure,sport,social,rythme,interets[]} or {off:true}. Siblings: 30225 avatar appearance (morph sliders), 30226 avatar photo (IPFS cid), 30227 directory entry ('infinity-annuaire').
identified.notes: Self-describing and no public source was found.

identified.name: Bro order status update
identified.app_or_protocol: Bro (Quizzicarol/bro-app, Brostr/bro) - pay Brazilian bills (PIX/boleto) with bitcoin
identified.what_it_is: Order-status update in Bro's bill-payment marketplace. `d=<orderId>_<pubkey8>_update` (or `_billcode`), `t=bro-order`, `t=bro-update`/`bro-billcode`, `t=status-<x>`, `r`/`orderId`=order UUID, `p`=provider and user, and `expiration` 30 days. The content is JSON `{type:'bro_order_update', orderId, status, providerId, userPubkey, publishedBy, paymentProof, updatedAt}`; billcode variants carry a NIP-44 `billCode_nip44` field. Other events in the family: 30078 order, 30079 accept, 30081 complete, 30082 provider profile, 30085 review. Some events (`model`, `prompt_hash`, `world` tags with imageUrl JSON) appear to be a second, unrelated app reusing 30080.
identified.notes: Bro's order kind 30078 collides with NIP-78 app data. 7 authors.

identified.name: Unidentified blinded hourly commitment
identified.what_it_is: Addressable event with `d=<64-hex>` (sometimes shared by several authors), `commit=<sha256>`, `scheme=sha256-blind/1,nip44/2`, `window=3600`, `epoch=<floor(unix/3600)>`, and `expiration` about 24 h. The content is NIP-44 v2. It looks like an hourly commit-reveal or blinded-presence scheme in which the commitment is public and the opening is encrypted to someone.
identified.notes: 7 authors. The epoch number equals the current hour index, which confirms the 3600 s window semantics.

identified.name: Infinity directory entry (annuaire)
identified.what_it_is: Addressable event with d='infinity-annuaire' and t='infinity-annuaire'. JSON content {v:1, nom (display name), joignable (reachable: bool), avatar?}. It is the user's opt-in listing in the app's member directory.
identified.notes: Same authors also publish 30051 (profile/passport) and 30052 (approximate position) with French vocabulary (territoire, compétences, abondance, passeport). Public project not found.

identified.name: Contested kind: Bro order completion, plus other apps
identified.app_or_protocol: Bro / Brostr (P2P bill-pay / PIX for sats); also 'nostrwall', 'verge:shares', an unknown encrypted 'announce'
identified.what_it_is: Several apps use this addressable kind. (1) Bro: kindBroComplete = 30081 (orders 30078, accept 30079, payment proof 30080, provider tier 30082). d='<orderId>_complete' or '_invoice_refresh', t='bro-order'/'bro-complete'/'bro-invoice-refresh', orderId, p (user), e (order event), expiration. JSON content has type, orderId, providerId, providerInvoice (bolt11), and proofImage or proofImage_nip44. (2) 4 events with t='announce', a 32-hex d and opaque (non-NIP-44) base64 content. (3) L='nostrwall' with d='bookworm', a curated list of 'e' tags with timestamps. (4) d='verge:shares' with JSON {shares:[]}.
identified.notes: Bro also uses 30078 for orders, which collides with NIP-78 application-specific data, so Amethyst's NIP-78 handling will see Bro orders. Its PIX bill payments put payment data on public relays (partly NIP-44 encrypted).

identified.name: PNS private note (Private Note Storage)
identified.what_it_is: Encrypted private storage of the user's own notes and settings. pns_key = HKDF(device key or nsec, salt 'nip-pns'). The outer kind-1080 event is signed by a keypair derived from it, has NO tags, and its content is NIP-44 v2 under a symmetric key derived from the same secret. The plaintext is an inner Nostr event: an unsigned rumor by the real pubkey, or a signed event. Clients find their notes by querying kind 1080 authored by their derived PNS pubkey.
identified.notes: Open NIP PR #1893 (jb55). nostrdb already auto-unwraps 1080. Useful to Amethyst for private drafts/settings backup synced across devices. 102 events from 7 derived keys, ciphertext 387-707 bytes, consistent with rumors.

identified.name: Infinity avatar appearance
identified.app_or_protocol: unidentified French 3D-avatar app (same author cluster as DATASPACE, data-space.world)
identified.what_it_is: Addressable avatar-customization record: d=<author pubkey>, t='infinity-avatar-apparence', visibility='public', expiration about 7 days. Content JSON (French field names) of body and face morph parameters: genre, modele, stature, epaules, hanches, teinte, carnation, peau, tenue, tailleCm, ageAns, and a 'formes' map of slider weights (menton-*, levres-*, machoire-*, muscle+/-...).
identified.notes: The same 7 authors publish 30218, 30226, 30227, 30228, 30051, 30052, 30215, 30197 and 30210. That is one French ecosystem ('Infinity' / 'Biosenger'), possibly built around DATASPACE (data-space.world, a French private-relay and storage service). App not publicly documented.

identified.name: Cryptographic Identity Proof (NIP-C1 draft)
identified.what_it_is: Links a non-Nostr signing key (an Android APK-signing X.509 certificate) to the Nostr pubkey that publishes apps. d=<SHA-256 of the certificate's public key>, `signature` = base64 signature by that certificate key over the attestation (256 bytes, i.e. RSA-2048), `expiry` = unix time about 1 year out. Content empty. Zapstore uses it to check that a release's APK signer belongs to the publishing npub.
identified.notes: Draft 'NIP-C1' per Zapstore code (not merged). It is on Zapstore's relay allow-list next to 32267/30063/3063. Relevant if Amethyst ever verifies Zapstore app releases.

identified.name: OC encrypted mailbox ('boîte') / probe
identified.what_it_is: Regular event, x tag = mailbox id ('oc-boite-<32hex>') or probe id ('oc-sonde-…', 'oc-sonde-boite-8571-<date>'), optional expiration (~3 weeks). Content either 'OCB1.' + base64url(0x04 || 64-byte uncompressed EC pubkey || ciphertext) — ECIES-style sealed message — or plain base64 ciphertext for probes. Looks like an anonymous drop-box messaging system that is also testing relay retention ('sonde' = probe).
identified.notes: 31 events / 6 authors; d-less, so x acts as the routing key.

identified.name: Grab-bag addressable (Snapstr read-state, kernl instance, job status)
identified.what_it_is: Mixed: (a) Snapstr: d 'Snapstr-Reads', client snapstr.app, NIP-13 PoW nonce tag ['nonce',n,'12'], NIP-44 content — encrypted per-user read/seen state; (b) kernl: d=<instance pubkey>, t 'kernl-instance', version, supports [directories, subs, posts, forums], content {schema, version, supports, active_at} — a server/instance advertisement; (c) d=<event id>, e=<same>, status 'completed' — a job-status marker tied to a kind 5101 result.
identified.notes: 7 events / 6 authors.

identified.name: Encrypted metadata / file record (Formstr Drive)
identified.what_it_is: Generic addressable 'metadata event' whose content is NIP-44 JSON encrypted to the author (or to a drive key). The `d` tag depends on the subtype: for the `files` subtype `d`=SHA-256 of the encrypted Blossom blob, and the plaintext holds name/size/type/folder/server/per-file key/chunks for a private encrypted drive. Samples show `d`=sha256 hex and ~220-byte NIP-44 content, without the `t` subtype tag the draft asks for.
identified.notes: PR 2412 is by Formstr dev 'rama' (geralt-debugs). The samples omit the `t`/`encrypted`/`client` tags, so the match is on shape.

identified.name: Video view (legacy NIP-71)
identified.what_it_is: Video view event from an earlier NIP-71. Tags were `a`/`d`=<34235|34236 coordinate of the viewed video>, optional `e`, and `viewed` start/end seconds, with an optional note as content. Live samples are sparse: mostly just an `e` tag (no `d`), and one with `d`/`a`=`22:<pubkey>:` (pointing at a kind-22 short video). Content is empty.
identified.notes: The kind was removed from NIP-71 in Oct 2024 and survives in a few clients. It is view/watch-history telemetry and not worth rendering.

identified.name: Unidentified group-scoped NIP-44 message
identified.what_it_is: Regular event with a single `h` tag holding a 40-hex (20-byte, SHA-1/RIPEMD-sized) group id that is the same across all 6 authors, plus an `expiration` of 14 or 60 days. The content is NIP-44 v2 ciphertext. It looks like a small closed group's encrypted message or state stream that uses NIP-29-style `h` scoping without NIP-29 kinds.
identified.notes: Single group observed.

identified.name: anonymate room join/leave marker
identified.what_it_is: Addressable membership marker: `d=<room/session UUID>`, `app=anonymate`, `action=join|leave`, with empty content. Each user keeps one event per room and the latest action wins. It is a public presence/membership signal for an anonymous-chat app.
identified.notes: Self-describing via the `app` tag. 6 authors.

identified.name: Infinity persona approximate position
identified.what_it_is: Addressable event with d = the author's pubkey, visibility='public', t='infinity-persona-position'. JSON content {lat, lng, approx:true, prec (meters, ~25-30 km), decl:true, at (ms)}: a deliberately coarsened self-declared location for a member map.
identified.notes: A privacy-conscious design: positions are blurred to tens of km. Companion of 30051/30227.

identified.name: Agent Reach heartbeat (plus one-off service catalogue)
identified.app_or_protocol: Agent Reach (AustinEral/agent-reach) — AI-agent discovery; also BlindOracle
identified.what_it_is: Agent Reach heartbeat: addressable (d='<id>-v1'), with NIP-32 labels L='agent-reach' and l=['heartbeat','agent-reach'], s='available', content {"status":"available"}. It marks an AI agent online; its capabilities are in the paired kind 31990 'Service Card'. One other author (BlindOracle) used 31991 for a JSON service catalogue (d='blindoracle-v1-catalogue', t service-catalogue, x402 USDC pricing).
identified.notes: COLLISION: Agent Reach puts its Service Card on kind 31990, which is NIP-89's handler-information kind. Amethyst's NIP-89 code may see those cards; they can be told apart by the L/l 'agent-reach' labels.

identified.name: imgtr image chunk
identified.what_it_is: Addressable chunk of an image: d '<shortid>:<n>', chunk <n>, sha256 of the chunk, e → the manifest event. Content is raw base64 of the image bytes (first chunk begins with the PNG signature 'iVBORw0KGgo'), ~28 KB per chunk. Manifest is sibling kind 30303 (t 'imgtr', d <shortid>, sha256, mime; content {protocol:'imgtr', version:2, filename, mime, size, width, height, sha256, chunks, pubkey}).
identified.notes: Uses relays as blob storage (78 events / 5 authors). Not encrypted (3 NIP-44 outliers). Could be rendered if ever popular, but Blossom is the supported path.

identified.name: Opaque addressable blob (d = t = 32-hex id)
identified.what_it_is: Addressable, d and t both equal the same 32-hex id; content is ~880 chars of base64 ciphertext (659 bytes, no NIP-44 version byte). Each author republishes a small number of ids. Looks like an app's encrypted record/state slot made discoverable by its id via the t tag.
identified.notes: 14 events / 5 authors.

identified.name: UPlanet DID document
identified.what_it_is: Addressable W3C DID document for a did:nostr identity. Public form: d 'did', t 'uplanet','did-document', schema 'https://www.w3.org/TR/did-core/', published_at, email, contractStatus (e.g. active_rental, cooperative_member_satellite, astroport_captain). Content is a DID JSON-LD doc {@context, id:'did:nostr:<hex>', alsoKnownAs:[mailto:, did:g1:…, /ipns/…], verificationMethod, authentication, assertionMethod, keyAgreement, service, metadata}. Private form: d=<uuid>, encrypted 'nip44', NIP-44 content.
identified.notes: 6 events / 5 authors. Publishes users' email addresses in a public tag. Related kinds seen from same authors: 30801, 31903, 10600. No NIP PR found; did:nostr itself is a separate W3C CG draft.

identified.name: BetPod FROST oracle key-refresh commit
identified.app_or_protocol: BetPod (prediction markets with FROST threshold oracle)
identified.what_it_is: Regular event, empty content, from each oracle node: frost-id (participant index as 32-byte hex), edition, base (old group key), new (refreshed group key), t 'betpod-oracle' and 'betpod-frost-refresh:<edition>'. Part of a FROST proactive key-refresh ceremony; siblings 4263 (round1 commitments), 4246/4251/4252/4264 and 30421 (oracle node registration: LLM model, roles) from the same keys; 4247 escrow-recovery records.
identified.notes: 5 events / 5 authors (one per signer).

identified.name: Sidestr chain tip / headers announcement
identified.app_or_protocol: sidestr (Bitcoin sidechain over Nostr, Melvin Carvalho; 'NIP-333')
identified.what_it_is: Tip announcement of a chain: `d`=`n`=chain alias (`sidestr:<name>` or `btc` for Bitcoin itself), `t`=sidestr, `tip`=height, `u`=mirror URLs serving the block file, `peg`, `e`=the kind-3500 chain document, and `alt`. Content is the hex of the last 12 block headers (80-byte SHA-256d or 164-byte BLAKE2b v2). One sample from 'holdbtc' reuses the kind for an unrelated game score attestation.
identified.notes: The sidestr reference code is AGPL-3.0, so do not copy it into Quartz without a licence check. The holdbtc 33333 is a collision.

identified.name: Encrypted sharded blob (unidentified)
identified.what_it_is: Addressable events with `d`='0.0'/'1.0' (index-like) and `t`=random 16-byte hex (a group/session id). Content is base64 binary: 0x01 version, u32 little-endian timestamp (≈created_at), padding/counter, then a 0.1-4 KB ciphertext. A few authors publish in lockstep.
identified.notes: Sibling 35713 (d=t=16-byte hex) is probably the same app.

identified.name: v1 f-tagged encrypted message (unidentified)
identified.what_it_is: Regular event with `v`=v1 and `f`=<32-byte hex>. Content is base64 starting with version byte 0x01 (not NIP-44 v2), ~450 bytes. Sibling 1002 adds `o` (other party), `i` (UUID session) and swaps o/f between two authors within seconds, which looks like a handshake/signalling exchange. Sibling 1000 has JSON arrays of byte arrays.
identified.notes: Kinds 1000-1002 sit in the regular range and could collide with future NIPs.

identified.name: imgtr image manifest
identified.app_or_protocol: imgtr (images stored as chunked relay events)
identified.what_it_is: Manifest for an image stored entirely on relays. `d`=6-char id, `t`=imgtr, `sha256`, `mime`. Content is JSON {protocol:'imgtr',version:2,filename,mime,size,width,height,sha256,chunks,pubkey}. The bytes live in kind 30304 chunk events (`d`=`<id>:<n>`, `chunk`, `sha256`, `e`=manifest, base64 content).
identified.notes: Blob storage on relays. Also collides with NIP-BB 'Book' chapter (PR 2248) and GammaMarkets escrow-service (PR 2334/2335) drafts that both use 30303.

identified.name: Pact HTLC atomic-swap offer
identified.app_or_protocol: Pact protocol / Satchel wallet (PoC-Consortium/satchel) - BTC <-> Bitcoin PoCX (btcx) swaps
identified.what_it_is: Addressable public order-book offer for a cross-chain HTLC swap. `d=<swap_id>` (16 hex), `network`, `give`/`get` asset tags, and NIP-40 `expiration` = created + ttl. The content is a separately BIP-340-signed envelope `{v:1, type:'offer', swap_id, from, body:{give_asset, give_amount, get_asset, get_amount, protocol:'pact-htlc-v1', t1_secs, t2_secs, ttl_secs, wire}, sig}`. The rest of the handshake (take/init/accept/funded/redeemed/abort) travels in NIP-59 gift wraps.
identified.notes: 5 authors. Comparable in purpose to NIP-69 P2P orders, but with its own envelope.

identified.name: Routstr provider announcement (+ lnproxy-v1 collision)
identified.app_or_protocol: Routstr (pay-per-request AI over Cashu) RIP-02; also an `lnproxy-v1` Lightning invoice-wrapping service
identified.what_it_is: Routstr form: addressable provider info with `d=<provider id>`, `u` endpoint URLs (https + .onion), `mint` (accepted Cashu mints), `version`, and kind-0-style content `{name, about}`. Users recommend providers with NIP-87 kind 38000 using `k=38421`. A second shape comes from `d=lnproxy-v1`: `n=<network>`, NIP-13 `nonce`, `expiration`, and JSON content with fee schedule, features (pay_bolt11, wrap_bolt11...), relays, onion URLs, node_pubkey and node_sig, advertising an LN proxy node.
identified.notes: Sovran's discovery code notes explicitly that kind 38421 is shared with lnproxy-v1. 5 authors.

identified.name: maxplayer Cashu cross-mint trade listing
source_urls: https://github.com/MakePrisms/maxplayerai (uses kinds 23410/23411 for its mint RPC)
identified.what_it_is: Public trade offer to swap ecash between two Cashu mints. Tags: `t=maxplayer`, `v=1`, `g`=give mint URL, `w`=want mint URL, `u`/`x`=units, `expiration`. The content is JSON `{trade_v:1, give:{mint_url, unit, net}, want:{...}, maker_trade_pubkey, expires_at, deadline_policy, fee_policy:'sender-funds-net-v1'}`. Most observed events are `t=maxplayer-trade-probe` relay-capability probes with content `{diagnostic: '... NOT a listing', trade_v:0}`.
identified.notes: The attribution to MakePrisms rests on the `maxplayer` name and that repo's adjacent 23410/23411 Cashu mint kinds. Only 5 events, mostly probes.

identified.name: Unidentified d=info encrypted record
identified.what_it_is: Addressable `d=info` record per author. The content is about 125 bytes of base64url starting with version byte 0x01, with variable lengths of 123-126 bytes, so it is not NIP-44 (which pads). It is probably a custom AEAD (e.g. XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a version prefix) holding a small per-user info blob.
identified.notes: 5 authors. The crawl labeled 2 of them nip44, but the shape matches none of NIP-44's padding.

identified.name: CI Job Result
identified.app_or_protocol: ngit-ci / NIP-C1 working draft (also implemented by Hive-CI-aligned 'rig')
identified.what_it_is: Regular event signed by a CI compute provider with the result of one CI job run for a NIP-34 repo: 'a' = repo coordinate(s) 30617:..., 'c' commit, 'w' workflow file path + hash, 'o' trigger (push/pull_request), 'job', 'name', 'conclusion' (success/failure), 'logs' (Blossom URL), 'artifact' (Blossom URL, filename, release), queued_at/started_at, 'r' ref, 'q' pointing at the 39842 Workflow Progress, plus NIP-22-style E/K/P and e/k/p tags for the PR or patch. Content is the log tail. Family: 9840 manual trigger, 9842 workflow result, 9843 service request, 9844, 19843 coordinator advert, 29846 secret update, 39842 workflow progress.
identified.notes: Gitworkshop renders these as CI status badges on PRs and commits. Amethyst already has a NIP-34 git browser (quartz nip34Git, amy git), so CI status on PRs/patches is a natural add. The kind numbers are marked 'experimental placeholders' by ngit-ci.

identified.name: Unidentified 'CC' encrypted addressable records
identified.what_it_is: Addressable event with d tags 'cc1:<40-hex>:...', 'cc2:<40-hex>:{b|c|metas|m2026-08a|m2026-09b...}', 'cc3:...:r' and a 't' tag equal to the 40-hex id (a group/collection id). Content is a custom envelope 'CCD1.<keyid>.<alg>.<base64url ciphertext>' (also 'CCQ1.' and 'CCV1.' variants), which looks like an app-level encrypted document store (monthly shards 'm2026-09a', metadata 'metas'), shared by several pubkeys under one collection id.
identified.notes: No public source found for 'CCD1' or 'cc2:'.

identified.name: Unidentified encrypted group message (t=topic hash, e=anchor)
identified.what_it_is: Regular event: 't' = 64-hex topic/group hash, 'e' = an anchor event id, and short base64url ciphertext (100-200 chars) as content. Different authors post under the same t/e pair, so it reads as an encrypted group chat or comment thread keyed by a hashed topic.
identified.notes: Shares t-hash 7b105095... and e ids with kind 31909, so it is the same system.

identified.name: BetPod oracle FROST key-refresh round-1
identified.what_it_is: Regular event with empty content from members of a FROST threshold-signing oracle federation running a key refresh: frost-id (participant index, 32-byte hex), edition, round1 (hex commitment package), base (group/base key hash), coord-protocol='2', t='betpod-oracle' and t='betpod-frost-refresh:<edition>'.
identified.notes: FROST DKG/refresh coordination for a betting oracle in public, probably feeding DLC-style attestations. No public repo found.

identified.name: ngit CI workflow result
identified.what_it_is: CI Workflow Result signed by the CI coordinator for a NIP-34 repo. Tags: `a` = 30617 repo announcement(s); `c` = commit; `w` = workflow file path + SHA-256; `o` = trigger (push / pull_request / manual); `r` = ref, or NIP-22 E/K/P + e/k/p pointing to the 1618 PR / 1619 update; `conclusion` (GitHub-style success/failure/...); queued_at/started_at; `q` tags quoting each kind-9841 Job Result and the service request. Content empty.
identified.notes: Family: 9840 manual trigger, 9841 job result, 9842 workflow result, 9843 service request, 9844 service stop, 39842 workflow progress (expiring addressable). gitworkshop renders them as CI status on repos/PRs; Amethyst's NIP-34 views could show the same badge. Repos seen: soapbox.pub, gitworkshop, Amethyst-style android-lint/test jobs.

identified.name: unidentified German daily encrypted topic posts
identified.what_it_is: Addressable with d='<64-hex group id>:<topic>:<YYYY-MM-DD>' where the topic is a German word with '.de' (buero.de, online.de, risky.de, sport.de, herz.de, zukunft.de, unterwegs.de, damals.de) or '~own'. A t tag holds a 64-hex group hash. Content is base64url ciphertext (custom, not NIP-44).
identified.notes: Same authors use 31902 (d='<group>:<date>', short ciphertext), 31909 (per topic per day with an e tag) and 1019 (regular, t+e). Looks like an encrypted group journal/check-in app with daily per-topic slots. Not found publicly.

identified.name: MaxPlayer trade lot status
identified.what_it_is: Hash-chained trade-ledger update for a 'lot' (an item for sale). Content JSON {trade_v:1, lot_id:<event id of the lot listing>, seq, prev:<previous update id>, status:'sold'}; tags t='maxplayer', v='1', e=<lot id>. Most samples are relay capability probes (t='maxplayer-trade-probe', content {diagnostic:'... NOT a listing', trade_v:0}).
identified.notes: Paired with kind 3410 (same 5 authors, probably the lot listing). Very low volume, test-like.

identified.name: Betpod FROST key-refresh packages
identified.app_or_protocol: Betpod oracle (unidentified betting oracle using FROST threshold signatures)
identified.what_it_is: One FROST signer's distributed key-refresh round message. Tags: frost-id = participant identifier (32-byte scalar such as 0x...02), edition = refresh epoch (e.g. 970285, which looks like a block height), t='betpod-oracle' and t='betpod-frost-refresh:<edition>'. Content JSON {packages: {<recipient frost-id>: <NIP-44 ciphertext>}, commitments: ...}: per-recipient secret shares are NIP-44-encrypted, while the commitments are public.
identified.notes: Same 5 authors publish 4263, 4272, 4246, 4251, 4252 and 30421 (napstr catalogue kind!?), so it is a whole threshold-oracle protocol family. No public repo found.

identified.name: FIPS paid route / internet-exit offer
identified.app_or_protocol: FIPS mesh — paid exit nodes (app 'fips/paid-route-offer', likely OpenTollGate / fips-tollgate)
identified.what_it_is: Addressable offer, d 'internet-exit', app 'fips/paid-route-offer', v '4', NIP-40 expiration ~1h. Tags: service internet_exit, payment cashu_spilman (Cashu Spilman payment channel), price_msat_per_gb, mint (accepted mints, repeatable), max_channel_capacity_sat, channel_expiry_secs, free_probe_units, grace_units, receiver_pubkey, network_class, country, asn, ip, fips_endpoint, last_seen_unix. Content JSON mirrors it {offer_id, seller_npub, receiver_pubkey_hex, service, access, pricing, channel, location, ip_support, quality, fips_endpoints?}.
identified.notes: Not in FIPS's own nostr-events.md (which only lists 37195/21059/10050), so it is an extension by the tollgate/exit-node projects. 11 events / 4 authors.

identified.name: Binary-framed expiring blob (x-tag)
identified.what_it_is: Regular event from one-shot pubkeys, x <32-hex id> + expiration (~1 day). Content base64 of a binary frame: 0x01 0x00 0x10 then the 16-byte id equal to the x tag, then type/length fields and ciphertext (~170–230 bytes). The detector flags it as nip44 but it is a custom framed format. Looks like an app's transport/RPC message keyed by a session id.
identified.notes: 4 events / 4 authors, one shared x id.

identified.name: notestr encrypted note
identified.what_it_is: Addressable, d = 6-char random note id, optional notestr-base <event id> (the version the edit is based on). Content NIP-44 v2 self-encrypted note body (~6 KB). Sibling kind 34579 holds NIP-44 entries whose d is an 'a' pointer '33457:<pubkey>:<d>' (sharing/key records).
identified.notes: Name taken from the 'notestr-base' tag; no public source found. 4 events / 4 authors.

identified.name: Encrypted keyed record (unidentified, 30700-30703 family)
identified.what_it_is: `d`=16-byte hex. Content is base64url ciphertext with version byte 0x01 (not NIP-44 v2), 250-450 bytes, re-published frequently. Same authors also publish 30701 (`d`=info), 30702 (`d`=11-char base64url ids that look like YouTube video IDs) and 30703 (`d`=body).
identified.notes: This looks like one app's encrypted key-value store.

identified.name: Encrypted p-tagged record (unidentified)
identified.what_it_is: `d`=16-byte hex and `p`=recipient. Content is NIP-44 ciphertext (220 or 1116 chars), published in pairs at identical timestamps by different authors. Probably an encrypted invitation/handshake addressed to the p-tagged user.
identified.notes: There is no link to the French-language 30090/30093 kinds, which share a number range but not a shape.

identified.name: Encrypted p-tagged record (unidentified)
identified.app_or_protocol: unidentified (collides with NIP-91 draft channel definition)
identified.what_it_is: `d`=16-byte hex, `p`=recipient, NIP-44 content (~1.8-2.1 KB). It has the same structure as 30092. This is not the NIP-91 draft (PR 2191/2199) 'Group Channel Definition', which is relay-signed and public.
identified.notes: Collision with a proposed NIP-29-adjacent kind.

identified.name: Unidentified 'zeitgeist' encrypted document
identified.what_it_is: Addressable NIP-44 v2 self-encrypted document. The `d` is either `zeitgeist-main` or a random 30-hex id, which suggests a main document plus sub-documents of an app called Zeitgeist (notes/journal/feed-config style).
identified.notes: 4 authors. The only repo hit for 32123 is a coordinate inside commons GeoRelayDirectory (false positive).

identified.name: Unidentified daily per-user token
identified.what_it_is: Addressable event with `d=<64-hex>:<YYYY-MM-DD>` and `t=<64-hex>`. The content is 48 bytes of base64url, which could be a daily blinded token, encrypted check-in, or proof-of-activity record.
identified.notes: 4 authors, all on 2026-10-07.

identified.name: Bitflash mining pool descriptor
identified.what_it_is: Addressable 'rendezvous descriptor' that Bitflash pool nodes refresh every few minutes (BTF_POOL_KIND = 38503, d='btf-pool-2' or 'btf-pool-2-testnet', with a matching t). JSON content: name, btf (the node's '.btf' overlay address), fee_pct, hashrate, miners, blocks.
identified.notes: Miner discovery for a pool network. The max age is 3 minutes, so it is high churn.

identified.name: Infinity profile / passport
identified.what_it_is: Addressable event with d = the author's pubkey and tags visibility='public', lang='fr', access='mode1'. JSON content {updatedAt, profile:{territoire, displayName, alias, profession, devise, competences[]}, optional bio, gallery, abondance, passeport}. It is an extended skills/territory profile for a mutual-aid community directory.
identified.notes: Companion of 30227/30052. Exposes a skills list and region publicly.

identified.name: Unidentified encrypted daily record per domain
identified.what_it_is: Addressable event with d='<64-hex>:<domain or ~own>:<YYYY-MM-DD>' (e.g. 'unterwegs.de', 'risky.de'), 't' = 64-hex topic hash, 'e' = anchor event. Content is short base64url ciphertext. One record per member per domain per day under a shared group hash, so it might be per-site daily notes or ratings in an encrypted group.
identified.notes: German domains in the d-tag. No source found.

identified.name: Mostro dev-fee payment receipt
identified.what_it_is: Regular event that a Mostro instance publishes for every successful trade, recording the development-fee share it paid. Tags: order-id, amount (sats), hash (payment hash), destination (lightning address, e.g. dev@pay.mostro.foundation), network, y=['mostro', <instance name>], z='dev-fee-payment', expiration about 1 year. Content empty.
identified.notes: Transparency/audit log of Mostro's fee-sharing; little end-user value.

identified.name: Mycelium CandidateRelay dial announcement
identified.what_it_is: NAT-traversal rendezvous for a libp2p-style network. An ephemeral 'GhostID' key publishes an addressable event: d='dial:<self>:<target>', p=<target>, qel='candidate-relay', qel-backchannel=<wss relay>, qel-transports='nostr-ws', and 'expires' = now + 300 s. Content JSON {ecdh_public, type:'candidate-relay', version:1}. Peers then tunnel data over Nostr using kind 39406.
identified.notes: Uses a custom 'expires' tag instead of NIP-40 'expiration', so relays never purge these events. The docs are in Portuguese.

identified.name: TWENTY ONE esports clan
identified.app_or_protocol: TWENTY ONE esports (EINUNDZWANZIG Bitcoin community esports league)
identified.what_it_is: Addressable definition of a clan/team (d=slug). Tags: name, clantag (e.g. 'SVD', 'BMK'), picture, r = link to the Einundzwanzig meetup page, and p tags with roles ('captain', 'member'). Content is a free-text clan description; alt='Esports clan: <name> [<tag>]'.
identified.notes: Players join with kind 12150 and the league runs chess and Rocket League ladders with Nostr login. 32151 appears too. Small (4 authors) but public, human-facing data, and the alt tags render fine as a fallback.

identified.name: Icebreaker ICE-sighting alert

identified.name: nsite manifest snapshot

identified.notes: Quartz's nip5aStaticWebsites has RootSiteEvent (15128) and NamedSiteEvent (35128) plus SiteAggregateHash and a path resolver, but no 5128 class, and 5128 appears nowhere in the repo. It looks like the snapshot section of 5A landed after the package was written. The path/x/server tag parsers can likely be reused directly.
